# Vertical overlay: Arts, Entertainment, and Recreation

**Level:** NAICS 2022 sector 71 (parent vertical)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 711310 Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports and Similar Events with Facilities. Live event venue operator with ticketing.
**Primary system:** Ticketing and venue operations platform

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
State gaming regulators (e.g., Nevada Gaming Control Board / Nevada Gaming Commission) Casino cybersecurity, internal controls, licensing; National Indian Gaming Commission (NIGC) Minimum internal control standards for tribal gaming (25 CFR 543); FinCEN (Treasury) Bank Secrecy Act AML program, SAR/CTR for casinos and card clubs; FTC FTC Act Section 5 and COPPA for consumer-facing entertainment; CISA / DHS SRMA, Commercial Facilities Sector (Gaming, Entertainment and Media, Sports Leagues, Public Assembly, Outdoor Events subsectors)

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**PCI DSS v4.0.1**, PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law). Cris Santos Company operates a live event venue with ticketing here, so card payments are its most binding security obligation (PCI DSS is a contractual standard enforced through card brands, not law). Research note: the sector research chose Nevada Gaming Commission Regulation 5.260, which applies only to licensed gaming operators; use it instead if the venue includes a casino.
Source: https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/standards/pci-dss/

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Patron PII and player-loyalty data; Payment card data and cage/credit (marker) records; BSA/AML records (SARs are confidential), CTRs, KYC documents; Surveillance video; Online/sports wagering account data, geolocation; Children's data (family entertainment apps); Employee licensing/background data
- **Critical systems:** Casino management system (CMS) / slot accounting; Table games and sports-betting/iGaming platforms; Surveillance and access control; Cage, credit and kiosk/TITO systems; Ticketing and point-of-sale; Loyalty/CRM platforms; Hotel PMS integration (integrated resorts)
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** PCI DSS validation for card payments
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Ticketing platform breach exposing customer and card data
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** Dynamic ticket pricing and bot detection

## Notes
CISA Commercial Facilities Sector SRMA is DHS; subsectors include Gaming, Entertainment and Media, Public Assembly, Sports Leagues and Outdoor Events. Other states (e.g., New Jersey DGE) have their own gaming technical standards; they were not verified here. No sector-specific AI rules were verified. All 50 states, DC and the territories have breach notification statutes with differing triggers, deadlines and regulator-notice duties. They are not enumerated here.
